acceptance: A parametrised unit test covers UNCERTAIN, NOT_VALIDATED, NOT_RUN with all queries successful (non-failure label, not red), UNCERTAIN with one failed query (FAILED), FAILED (FAILED) and PASSED (PASSED); it fails on develop before the change
The console label and the CLI exit code agree for every status in NON_CLEAN_VALIDATION_STATUSES (checked by a test that iterates that set)
A local seeded TPC-H SF 0.01 DuckDB run that records summary.validation other than passed prints the non-failure label and exits 0
description:
## Problem
`ConsoleResultFormatter._determine_benchmark_status` (benchbox/cli/output.py, develop 9ac60f085f) treats every validation status other than PASSED and PARTIAL as a failure. A run whose queries all succeeded but whose row counts could not all be checked (`UNCERTAIN`, `NOT_VALIDATED`, `NOT_RUN`) is printed as `Benchmark Status: FAILED` in red. The exit-code path disagrees: `result_cli_failure_reason` (benchbox/core/results/status.py) does not treat those statuses as failures, and `result_unvalidated_reason` names them as unvalidated. Users see a red FAILED on a run that exited 0.

## Evidence
Seen 2026-11-15 on seeded TPC-H runs (`--seed 42`) and on SF 10 runs with no reference answers, which record `NOT_VALIDATED`/`UNCERTAIN`. Reproduce with `SimpleNamespace(total_queries=22, successful_queries=22, failed_queries=0, validation_status="UNCERTAIN", query_results=[])` passed to `_determine_benchmark_status`: it returns `("FAILED", "red")`.

## Change
Derive the console status from the same helpers the exit code uses: failed queries or a CLI-failure validation status give FAILED; an unvalidated status (`result_unvalidated_reason`) gives a distinct non-failure label such as UNVALIDATED in yellow; otherwise PASSED or PARTIAL as today. A fix was written and tested on 2026-11-16 in a closed PR (#4266, closed for an unrelated reason) and can be reused.

## Guardrails
- Do not change exit codes, `summary.validation`, or staging admission; this is display only.
- A run with any failed query or a FAILED/ERROR/INTERRUPTED/PARTIAL validation must still never print PASSED.
- Keep one source of truth: no new status list in output.py.

## Decision gate
No owner decision is needed for the display fix. Stop and ask if the chosen label would need a new status value in results, the schema, or the Explorer.

## Verification rubric
Pass only if: the console label equals the exit-code classification for every status; no run with a failed query prints anything but FAILED; the unit tests fail on develop without the change.
